However, when there is a blemish in the five points of articulation, the breath of prayer and Torah emerging from his mouth emerges with a blemish and adhesion, and it is impossible for it to be unified above, for "whoever has a blemish shall not approach" (Leviticus 21:18) - and so it says in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 227b), in these words: and just as those five wings of the lung are all open without adhesion, to receive this voice, so too the five repairs of the mouth must all be open without adhesion, in the five repairs which are: Alef-Chet-Heh-Ayin in the throat, Bet-Vav-Mem-Peh in the lips, Gimel-Yud-Chaf-Kuf in the palate, Dalet-Tet-Lamed-Nun-Tav in the tongue, Zayin-Samech-Shin-Resh-Tzadi in the teeth - and let the speech that is in them be without adhesion and hindrance at all - this is what is written (Genesis 24:15), "and it came to pass, before he had finished speaking, that behold, Rebecca came out" - this is prayer, which is speech, and concerning it is said, "if my prayer is fluent in my mouth, I know it is accepted; and if there is adhesion and it comes out mixed, I know it is unfit," because adhesion is a "treifah" [invalidating flaw] - to this point.

Now, with this introduction, we shall understand the verse, in saying "al tevahel al picha" - and the intent is that your mouth comprises the five points of articulation explained. And "tevahel" [be rash/confused] means that no blemish be found in them, which is "behalah" [confusion] and husk, and the husk is external - it is "al picha" [upon your mouth], which is extraneous and comes upon the five points of articulation. And my colleague, his honor Rabbi Moshe Biarokash, peace be upon him, said something fine concerning this - that it is known (Parashat Naso, page 134a) that from the supernal mouth emerges "hevel" [breath], as we explained above, and it means, "do not be rash" - that you not transform "hevel" [breath] into "behalah" [confusion], which is the husk.

Now, along the lines of explaining "al picha," they explained, of blessed memory, in Tanchuma, of blessed memory: this is what Scripture says, "do not be rash with your mouth, and let not your heart be hasty to utter a word" - these are people who curse the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He. Come and see, when the higher and lower beings were created, they were created with half the Name, as it is said (Isaiah 26:4), "for in Yah, the LORD, is an everlasting rock" - and why were they not created with the whole [Name]? Because the world is not worthy that the whole Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, be mentioned. Woe to the creatures who curse the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He - see what is written concerning offerings: "an offering to the LORD," "a burnt offering to the LORD" - it does not say "to the LORD, an offering; to the LORD, a burnt offering" - yet people curse and blaspheme My Name - therefore it is said, "do not be rash with your mouth." This explicitly teaches that they came to explain the word "al tevahel" through "al" [upon] - for the "behalah" [rashness] is the cursing and blaspheming, and it is extraneous, upon the mouth - which a person has no need of, for his mouth, certainly, was created for the need of the five points of articulation within it.

And it is further possible to say - it is known that the speech that comes to a person is from the Shechinah, as it is said (Exodus 4:11), "who has made man's mouth, or who makes him dumb," and so on, "is it not I, the LORD?" - and the word "Anochi" [I] can be explained as the supernal Shechinah and the lower Shechinah, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 74b), that concerning them it is said "Anochi Anochi" - but the main one is the supernal Shechinah, from where it is "Anochi Adonai Elohecha" [I am the LORD your God], as explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 256b) - and this means, do not blemish the measure that is "al picha" [upon your mouth], from where it came to be a mouth, for the five points of articulation are from the secret of the supernal Heh, and from there too the power of speech, as it is said, "or who makes him dumb," and so on. And if we explain this concerning the Shechinah, "and she is upon your mouth," we explain "is it not I, the LORD," as voice and speech - and the rest of the particulars of the verse also fit these measures.

And I heard from my teacher, peace be upon him, that a person's mouth is above ten [handbreadths], and if the voice and speech emerging from his mouth are in holiness, the Shechinah is immediately bound to it, for the Shechinah does not descend below ten [handbreadths] (Sukkah 5a). And along these lines the wording of the verse "al picha" is now precise, that the Shechinah is "upon your mouth," since your mouth is above ten [handbreadths] - and this is (Psalms 68:14), "though you lie among the sheepfolds [shefatayim]," which is explained in the Tikkunim (page 45a) as, that he should lay the Shechinah, who is "Em" [mother], between his lips ["sefatayim"], in order to unify her.

Further, we already copied in the Gate of Love, chapter 9, what Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him, said in his precepts (Zohar, Parashat Naso, page 122b), that the Shechinah is "the utterance of the mouth of the LORD," through whom man is sustained, in these words, in brief: and she is the breath that enters a person's mouth without toil and without effort - Heh, "when they were created." And in this teaching "al picha" fits well.

"And let not your heart be hasty to utter a word before God" - the matter is that speech emerges from the heart, as explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna several times (Parashat Naso, page 121b; Parashat Pinchas, page 227b), and in the Tikkunim (page 28a), in these words: the heart is a consuming fire, from the right ear of the heart, which corresponds to the liver, and from it speech emerges - this is what is written (Jeremiah 23:29), "is not My word like fire, says the LORD" - and were it not for the wings of the lung that fan upon the heart, it would burn up the whole body - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:35-: And therefore it says, "and let not your heart be hasty to utter a word," for from it speech emerges, and the speech emerging from it is judgment, as Rashbi explained, that the heart is fire, and concerning speech it is said, "is not My word like fire." And speech emerges "before God," which is judgment - for the essence of this world was created with judgment, as it is said (Genesis 1:1), "in the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth" - and when He saw that it could not endure, He joined with it the attribute of mercy (cf. Bereshit Rabbah 12:15) - however, this is only a joining in some measure, for its essence was created with judgment and stands upon judgment, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Tzav, page 30b), that every single day judgment hangs over the world, because the world was created and stands upon judgment.

And it is possible to say, in another way, concerning "before God," to teach us of providence, and that he should know that when he speaks, the King of kings of kings, God, hears our words - and as Rambam, peace be upon him, explained concerning fear (Guide for the Perplexed, part 3, chapter 52), that a person does not prolong his words before a king as he does when he is in his own house - and the King of kings of kings' regard is constantly upon us, and therefore it says, "let not... be hasty," and so on.

However, one must examine precisely, for ultimately this verse appears redundant in its matter - for "do not be rash with your mouth" means that he should not let speech out of his mouth quickly, and this is the same as "and let not your heart be hasty," and so on.

Therefore it appears that these are two divisions: the first concerning worldly matters and the second concerning matters of holiness. Concerning what pertains to worldly matters it says, "do not be rash with your mouth" - meaning that although you have permission to speak, this being "your mouth," which is in your own domain, it should not be with rashness and haste, but with calm composure. And even concerning matters of holiness, when you stand before God, "do not be hasty to utter a word before God" - and so it is explained in the Talmud (Berachot, chapter 5, mishnah 1), that one should not pray immediately, but settle his mind first and know before whom he stands, as they said, "one may only stand to pray in a state of gravity," and so on. And so it says in the Midrash (Yalkut Shmuel 2, chapter 7, siman 146) that David said, I would not pray before God until I had settled my mind - and we shall copy his whole wording below concerning the matter of prayer, with God's help. And even in the occupation with Torah, one must sit in awe and direct his intent to what he utters from his mouth, as we shall elaborate in its place. And in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit, page 2a) it says that a word is worth a sela, but silence two [selas] - this applies even concerning Torah. And this is "and let not your heart be hasty to utter a word before God" - meaning, when you stand before the Shechinah, which is when he is occupied with Torah and prayer, let him not be hasty.

"For God is in heaven and you are on earth" - it is known that "Elohim" is a term of judgment and a judge, as they explained, of blessed memory (Shemot Rabbah 3:6), "when I judge My world I am called Elohim." And in saying "in heaven," it means that He judges in heaven with the whole heavenly retinue that is in heaven - and therefore it did not say "for God is above the heavens," which would indicate His removal and elevation from them, but rather "in heaven" is to watch over and judge, as (Psalms 103:19), "the LORD has established His throne in heaven, and His kingdom rules over all." Further, "Elohim" totals the numerical value of "ha-kisei" [the throne] - and this means that His throne, from which He judges, is in heaven, and the angels before Him, some on the right for merit, some on the left for guilt - and since, when a person speaks, the Holy One, blessed be He, judges his words with the whole heavenly retinue, whether his words are upright or not, it is fitting that they be few, in order to minimize the judgment upon him.

And therefore it says everything in the term "Elohim," for everything is judged with strict judgment, without leniency in anything - and as they said in the Midrash, Vayikra Rabbah (Parashat Emor 26:7), in these words: Rabbi would recite the verse, and when he reached this verse he would weep: "for behold, He who forms the mountains and creates the wind, and declares to man what is his speech [sicho]" (Amos 4:13). What is "declares to man what is his speech"? Rabbi Huna in the name of Rabbi Ye'avetz said, "who forms the mountains and creates the wind." Rabbi Huna in the name of Rabbi Ye'avetz said another interpretation: "tohu, choshech, va'afelah" [chaos, darkness, and gloom] - even matters that have no substance, even light conversation a person converses with his wife, are written on a person's record and read before him at the time of his death. And who writes them? "He who makes the dawn darkness" (Amos, ibid.) - to this point, their wording. And the reason speech is written by the blessed Name is because speech is through the soul, as it is written (Genesis 2:7), "and man became a living soul," and we translate [in the Targum], "and man became a speaking spirit" - and it is known that the soul is from Him, blessed be He, as it is written (ibid.), "and He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life" - and therefore, since the essence of the soul is what blemishes through speech or is repaired through good speech, everything is written by Him, blessed be He, in order to punish it or reward it, measure for measure, according to His blessed knowledge, which is not known to any creature, not to an angel and not to a seraph.

"And you are on earth" - it is precise in saying "and you are on earth," and not "and you are in the earth," along the lines of saying "for God is in heaven," to answer for us the difficulty we examined above. And the matter is that man's primary dwelling, before the sin of the first man, was in the Garden of Eden, removed from the coarse materiality of this turbid body - however, through his sin he was clothed in the body and matter of this world, and behold, according to his understanding he is separated from holiness. However, there the Holy One, blessed be He, placed in man, at the beginning of his creation, speech, beyond all the living creatures of this world, for through speech he is equal to the angels - and as explained above, the matter of the three bonds that are in man, nefesh, ru'ach, neshamah, which are deed, speech, thought - and Rashbi explained that speech is from the holy living creatures, which is the level of ru'ach (Tikkunei Zohar, page 68b) - and through speech there is power in man to cleave to holiness.

And this is what King Solomon, peace be upon him, intended in saying (Ecclesiastes 3:21), "who knows the spirit of the sons of man, whether it goes upward, and the spirit of the beast, whether it goes downward to the earth" - for man, from the aspect of the speech within him, his spirit ascends upward, while the beast's spirit descends downward, because it returns to its foundation in "Asiyah" [mere doing], since the power of speech was not placed in it, which is a divine power given to man, as it says (Genesis 2:7), "and He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living soul," and we translate, "and man became a speaking spirit."

And this is what it says, "and you are 'al' [upon/removed from] the earth" - for from the aspect of the soul and speech within you, you are removed from the earth and from its matter, meaning that you are not equal to the other living creatures of the earth. And therefore, when a person speaks, whether words of holiness or of the profane, he should not think that he is speaking on earth and that he is physical, but rather that he is spiritual, speaking with the angels, for in speech he is equal to them. And therefore the verse did not need to say "for God is in heaven and on earth," for where it would say that His providence is on earth, that is to watch over the deeds done on earth from the aspect of the material deed - but concerning speech, man is bound above, and immediately upon uttering speech he is "before God," for this God is in heaven. And this is the precision of the verse, "do not be hasty to utter a word before God" - and since "before God" might imply one who dwells on earth, it guards against this and says that God, whom I told you is in heaven - and you, when you utter speech, are removed from the earth ["al ha-aretz"] - it follows that you are speaking before God in heaven, for the reason stated.

"Therefore let your words be few" - since you stand above, before the King, it is not fitting that you prolong your words before Him. And it is precise in saying "your words" - meaning the words of the body, which are yours, and not the Holy One, blessed be He's - but words of praise, prayer, and Torah, which are His, the King desires that they always be before Him, to prolong His praises and meditate on His Torah.

And we have necessity for the reality of this introduction from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, that speech has this virtue more than other commandments a person performs - for the other things a person does in deed, there are seven, "the eyes of the LORD roam through all the earth," as explained in the Sabba, Parashat Mishpatim (page 107a), concerning (Psalms 51:6), "and have done evil in Your sight" - that they go about the world and through them every commandment or transgression a person performs is imprinted. However, concerning speech, Rashbi explained that the voice itself ascends above and is examined there, so he explained in the Zohar, Parashat Lech Lecha (page 92a), in these words: Rabbi Yosi opened (Isaiah 60:21), "and your people, all of them righteous," and so on - happy is Israel, more than all the other nations, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, called righteous - for we have learned, one hundred twenty-eight thousand masters of wings go about and fly through the whole world, and hear a voice and take hold of that voice - as we have learned, there is no matter in the world that has no voice, and it goes and flies in the firmament, and the masters of wings take hold of it and raise that voice to their Masters of judgment, and they judge it, whether for good or for evil, as it is written (Ecclesiastes 10:20), "for a bird of the heavens shall carry the voice," and so on - to this point. Behold, they said that every utterance has a voice and ascends above into the firmament, and from there the masters of wings take the matter.

And in the Zohar (Parashat Metzora, page 55a), on the verse (Psalms 17:1), "hear, O LORD, my just cause," and so on, "without lips of deceit" - they add and say that the voice itself ascends and splits the firmament, they said, of blessed memory: what is "without lips of deceit"? Rather, we have learned this: every single word a person utters from his mouth ascends above and splits the firmaments and enters the place it enters, and there that word is examined, whether it is a fit word or not - if it is a fit word, they bring it before the holy King to do His will; and if not, they turn it aside to the Other Side, to arouse another spirit through that word - to this point. And so he explained at the beginning of Parashat Naso, and we shall copy it below, with God's help.

And so in the Zohar (Parashat Tzav, page 31b), it says there that a matter dependent on speech arouses speech above, and it says, in these words: and should you say, what does a word arouse? Rather, so it is written (Job... "davar dibber"), that word arouses another word above, and it is called "davar" - "the word [devar] of the LORD which was," "and the word of the LORD was precious," "by the word of the LORD the heavens were made" - for we have learned, that word ascends and splits the firmaments until it ascends to its place and arouses what it arouses - if good, good; if evil, evil - as it is written (Deuteronomy 23:10), "and you shall guard yourself from every [evil] word," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 10:48-: However, a difficulty for this matter arises from what is explained in the Tikkunim (beginning of page 131), that there are angels called "masters of wings," appointed over the voices of Torah, in these words: and there are precepts that depend on the mouth, appointed over the voices of Torah and over the utterances of which it is said (Ecclesiastes 10:20), "for a bird of the heavens shall carry the voice, and a possessor of wings shall tell the matter" - to this point. And he says further there (page 72), and the angels of whom it is said "for a bird of the heavens shall carry the voice" depend on voice, and "a possessor of wings shall tell the matter" depends on speech - to this point. And this is difficult - since the voice ascends and splits the firmament of itself, why would these angels be needed?

And it may be said that this ascending voice certainly has some physical aspect from the side of the person, who is in this physical "Asiyah," and therefore the masters of wings take hold of it in order to refine it through them, so that it ascend to the fitting place - if it is a breath of Torah or prayer, that it ascend higher and higher to unify; and if the ascending voice is a voice concerning worldly matters, they judge it according to need. And with this answer we must also explain what they said in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel, page 201b), that there are several angels who raise the prayer from firmament to firmament - why would they be needed? Rather, certainly in order to refine it from physicality, so that it ascend higher and higher to unify.

Further, it is possible to say "for God is in heaven," as it is written in the Ra'aya Meheimna (page 258a), in the secret of the Name Elohim, in these words: "Elohim" testifies to His divinity, that there is "Elohim" and "the God of gods," and He is God over all and there is no god over Him - to this point. And "in heaven" shall be understood by what is said in the Tikkunim (end of page 3), that the Cause over all shines in the ten sefirot of Atzilut, and so on, and in the ten spheres of the firmament, and does not change in any place. And this is the intent of saying "for God is in heaven" - meaning that His divinity and His light shine in all the heavens as one, in one equality, as it says, "that shines in the ten spheres of the firmament," and so on - and now this certainly indicates providence.

Further, it is possible that "for God is in heaven" - for it is known that "Elohim" is the supernal Imma, and her dwelling is in "heaven," which are the three Patriarchs - and the intent is that she decrees no decree except through a court of three, which are the three Patriarchs, so that the matter be judged to the right and to the left, and afterward the third decides - and along this pattern, a person who is on earth must, when he utters a matter, first weigh it in the scales of the intellect, to the right and to the left, and to a decision - and through this his words shall be few. And further I have hidden matters concerning this verse, written with me, and it suffices with what we have elaborated for practical benefit.

Now, the particular aspects explained in this verse obligate a person to minimize his words - whether in the aspect of the secret of "hevel" explained, or in the aspect of the five points of articulation fixed in his mouth, that there be no adhesion in them, or in the aspect of voice and speech, or in the aspect of the refinement of the voice and speech that ascend above to be judged, as explained, or in the aspect of the constant providence upon him - he must minimize his words in worldly matters.
And with this the chapter is concluded:

Let us come to explain, in a chapter of its own, how great is the virtue of one who guards his mouth and tongue, and how great the blemish - although we have already explained some in this chapter, in the next chapter we shall add teaching, with God's help. And we have divided the matter into a chapter of its own, in order to give the reader room between one chapter and the next.

It is written, "who is the man who desires life, who loves days to see good? Guard your tongue from evil," and so on (Psalms 34:13) - our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Avodah Zarah 19a, at the end): Rabbi Alexandri would proclaim, who wants life, who wants life? The whole world gathered and came to him. They said to him, give us life. He said to them, "who is the man who desires life," and so on, "guard your tongue," and so on, "turn from evil and do good." Perhaps a person will say, I have guarded my tongue from evil and my lips from speaking deceit, [so now] I shall indulge in sleep [idleness] - therefore Scripture says, "turn from evil and do good" - and "good" refers only to Torah, as it is said (Proverbs 4:2), "for I have given you good teaching; do not forsake My Torah" - to this point.

And this story is brought in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 16:2) in another manner, and my teacher, peace be upon him, wrote that what it says, that he understood the verse only through that peddler, is because the verse is doubled, saying "who is the man who desires life" and then saying "who loves days to see good" - and it is resolved through the peddler proclaiming, who wants life? - for the whole world came to him - and if for the life of this world a person pursues to obtain a remedy by which he shall live, all the more so is it fitting that he pursue the life of the World to Come. And the days, which should be his "lovers" for the repair of his soul, it is fitting that he not sin in them through his tongue, in a manner that they not turn against him into enemies and accusers - and this is "loves days," that the days themselves become his lovers, for his good in the World to Come.

And in the Zohar (Parashat Shemini, page 41a) this verse is explained, in these words: Rabbi Abba opened and said, "who is the man who desires life," and so on, "guard your tongue from evil," and so on, and it is written (Proverbs 21:23), "he who guards his mouth and his tongue," and so on. "Who is the man who desires life" - what is "life"? Rather, this is the life called the World to Come, and life dwells there - and therefore we have learned, "it is a tree of life" - a tree from that life, a tree planted in that life - and therefore it is written, "who is the man who desires life." "Who loves days to see good" - what are "days"? Rather, this is the Name of the holy King, which is bound to those supernal days called "the days of the heavens upon the earth" - "the days of the heavens," certainly, "upon the earth," certainly. Whoever wants the supernal life, to have a portion in them, and whoever wants the days, to cleave to them and love them, let him guard his mouth from everything, guard his mouth from food and drink that defiles the soul, and distance himself from those [things opposed to] that life and those days; let him guard his mouth from evil words, so as not to be defiled by them, and distance himself from them and have no portion in them. Come and see, mouth and tongue - another, supernal place is likewise called this - and therefore one should not blemish his mouth and his tongue, and all the more so not defile his own soul and body, because he is defiled in the other world - and this has been established.

And what appears to us in explaining the verse, by the plain meaning, in saying "who is the man" - in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, end of page 128a) it explains that whoever overcomes his inclination is called "ish" [a man] - and the reason he is called "man" who guards his tongue from evil is because the sin of the tongue is constant, and one who overcomes his inclination and does not speak at the time his inclination entices him to speak deserves to be called "man" - unlike other transgressions, where, even though he may overcome it once, it is not constant and does not raise him so much that he be called "man," as does one who guards his tongue.

And it intends to tell us the great virtue a person attains by properly guarding the tongue. The first is the cause of cleaving to his God, as explained, that these are the essence of life, and concerning this the righteous one is called "living" - "and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, son of a living man" (2 Samuel 23:20), and likewise "and the living shall lay it to his heart" (Ecclesiastes 7:2) - and as the poet said, "in my distance from You is my death in my life, but if I cleave to You, my life is in my death." And what follows from his desiring life is that he loves the days, for the days are supernal illuminations drawn down below for the repair of the soul, and the hidden treasure for the righteous is hidden and concealed within the days, and whoever refines himself merits to see his world in his lifetime, as they said in Berachot (17a), "you shall see your world in your lifetime" - and this is "to see good," meaning to see his world in his lifetime - and only one who properly guards his tongue attains this virtue, and this is what it says there in the teaching, "your mouth shall speak wisdom, and your tongue shall silence songs" - and everything mentioned in the teaching is all preparation for what is mentioned at the beginning of the teaching, "you shall see your world in your lifetime, and your hope for generation after generation."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 11:6-1: And it says, "guard your tongue from evil" - agreed upon in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit, beginning of page 57), that the word "ra" [evil] is applied to one who emits seed in vain, and he bases the matter on the verse (Genesis 38:7), "and Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil [ra] in the eyes of the LORD" - meaning that he would emit seed in vain - and this is his wording, in brief, on this matter: Rabbi Yosi said, is "ra" not "rasha" [wicked]? He said to him, no - a "rasha" is even one who raises his hand against his fellow, even though he does nothing to him, is called "rasha," as it is written (Exodus 2:13), "and he said to the wicked one [rasha], why do you strike your fellow" - it does not say "you struck," but "you strike" [future/ongoing] - but "ra" is called only one who corrupts his way and defiles himself and defiles the land - to this point, relevant here. Behold, it is explicit that he speaks in a negative formulation, "ra" is called only [such], and so on.

Now, along these lines it must be explained concerning the tongue - and the matter is that after it was explained that there are two covenants corresponding exactly to each other, the covenant of the tongue and the covenant of the flesh (end of Sefer Yetzirah, chapter 1, mishnah 2) - just as, with the covenant of the flesh, one who emits seed in vain is called "ra," so with the covenant of the tongue, one who emits a word in vain is like one who emits seed in vain, and therefore it says "guard your tongue from evil," so that you not be called "ra," who is the one who emits [in vain], as explained.

And it says "netzor" [guard, a stronger word] and not "shemor" [guard, ordinary] or the like, to indicate great guarding, a fence and a wall within a wall, as the word "netzor" indicates - and so Radak explains in Sefer HaShorashim, that "netzor" is from the root of "matzor" [siege/fortification], along the lines of (Deuteronomy 20:20), "and you shall build a siege-wall against the city" - and it is the most excellent guarding.

And so, in the word "netzor leshonecha" [guard your tongue], it does not say "netzor ha-lashon mera" [guard the tongue from evil], but "leshonecha" [your tongue] - meaning that you should see with the eye of the intellect that your tongue is surrounded by two walls, as they explained, of blessed memory (Arachin 15b), on the verse (Psalms 120:3), "what shall be given to you, and what more shall be done to you, you deceitful tongue" - the Holy One, blessed be He, said to the tongue: all of a person's limbs are upright and you are laid flat; all of a person's limbs are on the outside and you are on the inside; and not only that, but I have surrounded you with two walls, one of bone and one of flesh - "what shall be given to you," and so on - to this point. And this is the matter of "netzor" [guard], alluding to a hidden and concealed place, to indicate the siege-fortification of the two walls it has - and therefore the Creator concealed it with these concealments of the walls, which He did not do for the other limbs - and this is certainly because of its virtue, and it is like the parable of a person who stores his precious possession in a treasury within a treasury.

And to explain the matter, why one who emits seed in vain and one who emits a word in vain are both called "ra," the reason is what we explained, that the tongue is in the place of life, as explained above concerning "who is the man who desires life" - and just as the seed is a physical vitality in a person, being from the light of his eyes, and so on (Rambam, Hilchot De'ot, chapter 4, halachah 19), and it begets physically, as is known, and one who emits it in vain is called "ra" because of the secret and allusion above within it - so the matter of the tongue, which is the fortification of the secret of the spiritual vitality clothed in the vessel of the tongue, begets above in spiritual holiness, and it is not fitting for it to be emitted in vain - and this is the virtue of a rabbi who never engaged in idle talk all his days.

And although we said that "ra" is said of speech in vain, nevertheless anything blemished, that indicates an external force, is also called "ra" - and the proof is slander, which is harmful - and although some benefit might result from saying it, nevertheless it is called "ra" in itself, since the external force has a share in it - and the general rule of "guard your tongue" is: from any speech in which the external force, called "ra," has a share.

And it says "leshonecha" [your tongue] and "sefatecha" [your lips] in the second-person form, to indicate what they said, of blessed memory, in Bereshit Rabbah (67:3), that the mouth is in a person's own domain - that if he wishes he speaks Torah and good, and if he wishes he speaks evil - and this is "leshonecha" and "sefatecha," which are in your own domain. In these words: Rabbi Levi said, six things serve a person, three in his domain and three not in his domain. The ear, the nose, and the eye are not in his domain - he sees what he does not wish, hears what he does not wish, smells what he does not wish. The mouth, the hand, and the foot are in his domain - if he wishes he labors in Torah, if he wishes he curses, if he wishes he does not curse. The hand - if he wishes he abounds in commandments, if he wishes he steals and kills. The foot - if he wishes he goes to synagogues and study halls, if he wishes he goes to theaters and circuses. At a time a person is meritorious, the Holy One, blessed be He, makes those in his domain not in his domain - the mouth: "and he shall also be blessed" (Genesis 27:33); the hand: "and his hand dried up" (1 Kings 13:4); the foot: "my son, do not walk in the way with them," and so on (Proverbs 1:15) - to this point.

And it is written in Sefer Menorat HaMaor of Rabbi Yisrael, peace be upon him, that there are seven openings in the head, corresponding to the seven branches of the Menorah, and the mouth corresponds to the middle branch, which is holy - and therefore one must sanctify his mouth and tongue on the Sabbath day, which is the seventh and holy, for all sevenths are holy.

And in the Tikkunim (page 137a): "the Torah of truth was in his mouth" (Malachi 2:6) - this is the Sanctuary, and concerning it is said (Psalms 51:17), "O Lord, open my lips" - within it is the Holy of Holies, and this is the heart - to this point. And reason dictates that speech be sanctified, since it emerges from the Holy of Holies, which is the heart, to the Sanctuary, which is the mouth. And further you shall find that the word "kadosh" [holy], spelled out in full with the reckoning of its four letters, totals the numerical value of "dibbur" [speech], spelled out in full.

Further, it means "guard your tongue from evil" - that whoever blemishes his mouth with vulgar words and the like, they defile him and bring him to emit seed in vain, teaching him that he is "ra" - and as explained in the Zohar (Introduction, page 8a), on the verse (Ecclesiastes 5:5), "do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin," in these words: Rav Hamnuna Sabba said, "do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin" - that a person should not give his mouth to come to an evil lustful thought, and cause that holy flesh, sealed with the holy covenant, to sin - for if he does so, they lead him to Gehinnom, and the one appointed over Gehinnom, called Dumah, and how many myriads of destroying angels with him, stands at the gate of Gehinnom - and whoever guards the holy covenant in this world, he has no permission to approach him - to this point. And my teacher, peace be upon him, was precise in saying "that a person should not give his mouth to come," and so on - the intent being to be precise about the wording of the verse, which says "do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin," and so on - for the intent is not to warn us merely not to sin with the tongue, for if so it should have said "do not sin with your mouth" - rather, even words that contain no vulgarity of the mouth, but would lead to lustful thought, are forbidden - such as speaking with one's wife about matters of intercourse, which would lead to lustful thought and cause his flesh, which is the holy covenant, to sin, by emitting seed in vain.

And it is found from this that guarding the covenant depends on guarding the tongue, because they are two exactly corresponding covenants, as explained - and therefore Scripture puts guarding the tongue first, because it is the essential thing and includes the two hundred [i.e., is worth double] - for if he guards the tongue, the covenant is guarded of itself; but if he is not careful in guarding the tongue, even though he is careful in guarding the covenant, even the guarding of the covenant does not avail him - and the reason is explained in what we have said.

And so it is also explained in Parashat Noach and in Parashat Acharei Mot, that whoever blemishes with his tongue is defiled, and is found to be called "ra" - at the end of Parashat Noach (page 76a) he says, in these words: Rabbi Yosi opened and said (Deuteronomy 23:15), "for the LORD your God walks in the midst of your camp, to deliver you and to give your enemies before you; therefore your camp shall be holy, that He see no unseemly thing [ervat davar] among you, and turn away from you" - "for the LORD your God walks [mit'halech]" - it should say "mehalech" [simple form] - rather, as it is said (Genesis 3:8), "walking [mit'halech] in the garden in the cool of the day" - and this is the tree from which the first man ate - "mit'halech" is feminine, "mehalech" is masculine - and this is what goes before Israel when they went in the wilderness, as it is written (Exodus 13:21), "and the LORD went before them by day," and so on - it is what goes before a person when he walks on a road, as it is written (Psalms 85:14), "righteousness shall go before Him, and shall set his footsteps on the way" - and this is what goes before a person at the time he is meritorious. And why? "To deliver you and to give your enemies" - to save a person on the road and so that another [power] not rule over him.

And therefore a person must guard himself from his sins and purify himself - what is purification? "Therefore your camp shall be holy" - what is "holy" [kadosh, singular]? It should say "holy" [kedoshim, plural] - rather, "your camp shall be holy" refers to the limbs of the body, with which the body is joined and repaired, and therefore "your camp shall be holy." "That He see no unseemly thing [ervat davar] among you" - what is "ervat davar"? This is the nakedness of forbidden relations, for this is a matter the Holy One, blessed be He, despises more than anything. Since it says "that He see no ervah among you," why "davar" [thing/word]? Rather, these wicked ones of the world, who defile and befoul themselves with their own word [davar] that emerges from their mouths - this is "ervat davar" - and why so much? Because He goes before you, and if you act thus, immediately "and turn away from you" - so that He not go with you and turn away from you - to this point. And so in Vayikra Rabbah (Parashat Kedoshim 24:7): "that He see no unseemly thing [ervat davar] among you" - the nakedness of speech [ervat dibbur] - Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said, this is vulgar speech - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 9:22-1: And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, was further precise in his wording, saying, "and there ascend all aromas and incenses," and so on - the intent being that the incense too would ascend to this place to sweeten judgment, and also, if a person reads about the incense with intent, it shall ascend to this place to repair and sweeten the judgments - and at the end of Parashat Vayakhel (page 218b) they elaborated on the virtue of the incense, and we shall copy its wording concerning the matter of prayer, and from there is also proof for our intent.

And what it says, "and if not, they ascend," in love and fear - while above, concerning hearing, it mentioned only fear alone - the reason is that smell is on the central line, as it says, "smell there is [for] men of truth," and the attribute of truth unifies the left and the right, which are fear and love, and therefore the repair of the aroma of prayer, and everything that ascends to the nose, is through fear and love.
And with this the chapter is concluded:

After we have explained, in the previous chapters, sight, hearing, and smell, which correspond to Yud-Heh-Vav, lion, ox, eagle, as we copied the wording of Rashbi at the beginning of chapter 8, let us now explain speech, which corresponds to the final Heh, and is the face of man.

And the wording of Rashbi there (Ra'aya Meheimna, Parashat Pinchas, page 234a): "speech - man, who holds above and below." And the explanation of these words is explained in what is explained in the Tikkunim (page 122a) concerning the four repairs, which are sight, hearing, smell, speech - it explains there that sight is to the right, lion; hearing to the left, ox; smell in the middle, eagle - and he says afterward, in these words: the mouth, this is man, comprising four letters and comprising ten letters, and this is the Shechinah - to this point. And "comprising four letters," and so on, is the Name YHVH and Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud, and so he explained (page 129a).

And the matter shall be better understood from what he says in the Tikkunim (ibid., page 63a), that lion, ox, eagle are sight, hearing, smell, and upon them rests the supernal face of man, which is the secret of thought - and afterward he says, at the end of his words, "speech, this is man, who comprises them all - who brings it forth? Thought" - to this point. And through this teaching the two previous teachings shall be understood: what it says on page 121, that speech is the Shechinah, and it is in the secret of the simple and full Name spelled with ten [letters] - so it is true, that in it the Name is simple, from the side that it includes the three faces, which are lion, ox, eagle, Yud-Heh-Vav, within it, being the final Heh; and the Name is full with ten, from the secret of the supernal thought, as I elaborated above in chapter 6. And so speech too is found holding above and below - above, in the secret of thought, and below, in the Shechinah - this is the general understanding of the matter.

And in particular, a person does not speak except that he first thinks what he shall speak - rather, it is necessary that that speech be imprinted in thought first, and when he speaks, the power of thought goes out together with that speech - and therefore speech necessarily contains the two Names mentioned together, and this is the secret of (Proverbs 3:19), "the LORD founded the earth with wisdom" - and therefore it is explained in the Tikkunim (page 83a), in these words: Yud is speech, utterance, and reading.

However, it is difficult for me what is said in the Tikkunim, page 3a, that speech is the Name Adonai - and it is possible to say that what is said in the teaching before us, concerning the matter of YHVH simple and full, is entirely the aspect of voice [kol] - and this requires study.

And to understand the matter in its proper composition, it shall be explained by what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Noach, page 74a), on the verse (1 Kings 6:7), "and the house, when it was built, was built of stone made ready before it was brought there" - he explained this verse concerning the matter of speech, from where its root is, and explained that its root is from the secret of thought, and says: when the desire arises before the Holy One, blessed be He, to make honor for His own honor, will arises from within thought to spread, and so on. And he says [describes] the reality of the spreading of Atzilut until it becomes voice, and says, from where thought, which was sealed in silence, becomes audible so as to be revealed. Further, this thought spreads to become revealed, and this voice strikes and knocks upon the lips, and then speech emerges and completes everything and reveals everything - it is understood that everything is that sealed thought that was within, and everything is one; once this spreading arrives and speech is made with the strength of that voice, then "and the house, when it was built" - "when it was built" is not written, and so on - to this point, relevant here. And whoever wishes to delve into the secret of the matter should examine the teaching in its place there.

And similar to this he says in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi, page 246b), concerning (Genesis 49:21), "Naphtali is a hind let loose, who gives [feminine form] beautiful words" - he explained this verse in the secret of speech, and raised a difficulty that it should have said "hanoten" [masculine "gives"], and answered: come and see, thought is the beginning of everything, and so on - and at the end of his words he says, and when you examine the levels, it is thought, it is Binah, it is voice, it is speech, and all is one, and it is the very thought that is the beginning of everything, and there is no separation, but all is one, and one binding, which is literally thought, bound in Ein [nothing/Ein Sof] and never separated - and this is "the LORD is one and His Name is one" (Zechariah 14:9) - and therefore it is written "hanotenet" [feminine "gives"] - to this point.

And through the reason for the secret alluded to, we shall understand what is said in the Zohar (Parashat Chukat, page 183b), that one who guards his mouth and tongue merits to be clothed in the holy spirit, in these words: "and Esther put on royalty" (Esther 5:1) - that she was clothed in the holy supernal royalty, certainly she was clothed in the holy spirit. Why did she merit this place? Because she guarded her mouth not to reveal anything - this is what is written (ibid. 2:20), "Esther did not reveal her kindred" - and we learn that whoever guards his mouth and tongue merits to be clothed in the holy spirit - to this point. And in the Zohar (Parashat Acharei Mot, beginning of page 61), it explains that when it [the Shechinah, "zot"] is called the holy spirit, it is when she nurses from the secret of Chokhmah, in these words, in brief: and this "zot," when she is blessed, is called "kodesh" [holy] and called "Chokhmah," and they called her "the holy spirit" [ru'ach ha-kodesh], meaning a spirit [ru'ach] from that supernal holiness [kodesh] - to this point.

And the reason for the word "clothing" [hitlabshut], why one merits the holy spirit through guarding the tongue, shall be explained by what is explained in the Idra (Parashat Naso, page 134a), in the arrangements of the supernal beard, arrangement twelve, where it says that the holy spirit that emerges from the supernal mouth clothes Ze'ir Anpin, and from this spirit all those below are clothed, and so on. And he says afterward: and therefore the spirit that goes out and is clothed by the faithful prophets is called "the fruit of the LORD" - but in this Atika of Atikin [Ancient of Ancients] it is not separated, and none knows His spirit but Him - to this point.

And from here you shall know how great is the virtue of one who guards the spirit of breath emerging from his mouth, for it alludes to a supernal place, and therefore he merits to be clothed in the holy spirit. And concerning one who guards his spirit it is said (Proverbs 11:13), "but he who is faithful [ne'eman] in spirit conceals a matter" - and "ne'eman" is explained as being strong in his spirit, not to release it to an unfitting place, and the word "ne'eman" is explained as in (Isaiah 22:23), "and I will fasten him as a peg in a sure [ne'eman] place" - explained as strong, without wavering. And the opposite of this (Proverbs 29:11), "a fool releases all his spirit."
